title: Error boundaries in UI code (manual patterns)
learningObjectives: Explain error boundaries in ui code (manual patterns) and apply secure, accessible, maintainable browser practices.

understand.concept: Vanilla JavaScript does not provide a built-in React-style error boundary for arbitrary DOM subtrees. Applications can isolate rendering operations with try/catch, validate data at boundaries, and provide component-level fallback UI. Async failures need rejection handling as well.
understand.whyItMatters: A single malformed record should not blank an entire page. Isolate independent rendering regions and report errors without exposing secrets or internal stack traces to users.
understand.analogy: A component boundary is a fire door that contains a local failure and leaves other parts of the page usable.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; browser security, accessibility, and performance rules depend on platform behaviour and server configuration.

explain.narrative: The wrapper catches a synchronous rendering error and replaces only that panel with a safe message. Async work needs its own try/catch or rejection handler.

examples.code: function renderPanel(root,render){try{render(root)}catch(error){console.error(error);root.textContent='This panel could not be displayed.'}}
examples.explanation: The wrapper catches a synchronous rendering error and replaces only that panel with a safe message. Async work needs its own try/catch or rejection handler.
examples.expectedOutput: Browser console or UI output demonstrates the security or reliability principle.

practise.guidedTask: Create two independent panels. Force one renderer to throw and confirm the other panel remains usable.
practise.independentTask: Review a small browser feature for security, accessibility, performance, and lifecycle risks. Add a fallback and document the server-side controls required.
hints: Treat all browser and network input as untrusted.
Use exact origin checks and least privilege.
Measure performance and clean up resources.

questions.prompt: Does try/catch around a synchronous function automatically catch a later rejected Promise?
options: No, the Promise rejection must also be awaited or handled
questions.answer: No, the Promise rejection must also be awaited or handled
questions.explanation: A later asynchronous rejection requires await inside try/catch or a rejection handler.

questions.prompt: What is a sound browser engineering principle?
options: Defence in depth, least privilege, and usable fallbacks
Assume all browser features are always available
questions.answer: Defence in depth, least privilege, and usable fallbacks
questions.explanation: Secure and reliable interfaces combine trusted server enforcement with careful client behaviour.
